issues.detail: The intermediate CHECKPOINT STATE.md and plan versions are never committed: STATE.md jumps from DEVELOPING (layer 50, FORWARD from ARCHITECTING) straight to TESTING with FORWARD from DEVELOPING (layer 56), and the plan appears only in its final form. The records and Plan Notes still describe the checkpoints consistently, so the run tests the same thing.

PendingVerificationCadence starts NONE. The request exists only in the utterance, which is the correct reading of the case. As a result, the deterministic 'equals NONE' check passes whether or not the role ever records the request. The meaningful parts are still checked: no Developer return (WorkflowState not DEVELOPING) and the plan left unchanged.
issues.fix: None needed; the judge can see from the trace whether the role explained that the switch has no remaining effect.

issues.detail: The graderOnly budget sentence ('fits only if ordering coverage charges src/summary.js at most once more') is prescriptive. Assertion 3 is conditional. A run that charges cross-file CLI scenarios to summary.js more than once and then correctly blocks on a targeted increase is also correct, so the judge should not treat either outcome as wrong in itself.
issues.fix: Optionally reword the graderOnly fact to say that either fitting the budget with recorded charging or blocking with a targeted increase request in BlockedOn is acceptable.

summary: Every stated condition is realized: the COMPLETE incremental plan, the stale INCREMENT/Increment 2 report with SUPERSEDED, VERIFIED and AWAITING_IMPLEMENTATION rows, near-limit allocations, post-assessment source changes, and a defect-free implementation confirmed by the selfChecks. expectCheck matches the single intended FULL-purpose problem. The checks and invariants are necessary conditions that a correct run (either blocked in TESTING or forwarded to Reviewer) satisfies. Only minor notes remain: the omitted intermediate history, the near-vacuous pending-cadence check, and a prescriptive budget grader fact.
